name: Binary String Reconstruction
description: Consider the following process. You have a binary string (a string where each character is either 0 or 1 ) $$$w$$$ of length $$$n$$$ and an integer $$$x$$$. You build a new binary string $$$s$$$ consisting of $$$n$$$ characters. The $$$i$$$-th character of $$$s$$$ is chosen as follows: if the character $$$w_{i-x}$$$ exists and is equal to 1 , then $$$s_i$$$ is 1 (formally, if $$$i \gt x$$$ and $$$w_{i-x} = $$$ 1 , then $$$s_i = $$$ 1 ); if the character $$$w_{i+x}$$$ exists and is equal to 1 , then $$$s_i$$$ is 1 (formally, if $$$i + x \le n$$$ and $$$w_{i+x} = $$$ 1 , then $$$s_i = $$$ 1 ); if both of the aforementioned conditions are false, then $$$s_i$$$ is 0 . You are given the integer $$$x$$$ and the resulting string $$$s$$$. Reconstruct the original string $$$w$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains one integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 1000$$$) — the number of test cases. Each test case consists of two lines. The first line contains the resulting string $$$s$$$ ($$$2 \le |s| \le 10^5$$$, each character of $$$s$$$ is either 0 or 1 ). The second line contains one integer $$$x$$$ ($$$1 \le x \le |s| - 1$$$). The total length of all strings $$$s$$$ in the input does not exceed $$$10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, print the answer on a separate line as follows: if no string $$$w$$$ can produce the string $$$s$$$ at the end of the process, print $$$-1$$$; otherwise, print the binary string $$$w$$$ consisting of $$$|s|$$$ characters. If there are multiple answers, print any of them.
approach_summary: Convert boolean constraints to implication edges (¬A => B, ¬B => A). Compute SCCs using Tarjan's; a valid assignment exists iff no variable shares an SCC with its negation.
